subject: Re: Running Shiny Server on EC2 using community AMI isn't accessible via web

messages.author: bda90bcea347c4f0
messages.subject: Re: Running Shiny Server on EC2 using community AMI isn't accessible via web
parts:
Sorry I actually used my own security group that only allowed SSH access. 

I had to add a custom TCP rule for port 3838. All set now! Maybe this will help others!

On Monday, August 19, 2013 9:31:20 PM UTC-4, tcash21 wrote:
When I try to run shiny-server on the ShinyServer AMI provided by Jeff Allen I get the following error:
[2013-08-20 01:27:27.767] [INFO] shiny-server - Shiny Server v0.3.0 (Node.js v0.8.19)
[2013-08-20 01:27:27.769] [INFO] shiny-server - Using config file "/usr/local/lib/node_modules/shiny-server/config/default.config"
[2013-08-20 01:27:27.798] [INFO] shiny-server - Starting listener on 0.0.0.0:3838
[2013-08-20 01:27:27.804] [ERROR] shiny-server - HTTP server error (0.0.0.0:3838): listen EADDRINUSE

Here's the output of lsof -i :3838
node    1463 root    7u  IPv4   8800      0t0  TCP *:sos (LISTEN)

When I go to publicDNS URL of my instance at port 3838 it just times out. 

Any other information I can provide?

Listening on domain socket 41858 Error in startPipeServer(port, mask, httpuvCallbacks) : Failed to create server Calls: runApp -> startAppDir -> startApp -> startPipeServer Execution halted

I'm not finding any results by googling the above error message other than the httpuv source code.
